entries.label: Long-run effect of trade openness on (Harrod-neutral) multifactor productivity
entries.units: change in ln MFP per percentage point of GDP of trade openness (size adjusted)

citation.title: The quantification of structural reforms in OECD countries: A new framework
citation.publisher: OECD Economics Department Working Papers No. 1354, ECO/WKP(2016)78
citation.locator: Table 1, row 'trade openness (size adjusted)', columns (1)–(3), p. 10 (PDF p. 11); Table 4, row 'Openness (perc. of GDP)', p. 19 (PDF p. 20)

entries.quote: trade openness (size adjusted) 0.007** 0.008** 0.006** … Openness (perc. of GDP) 4.01 0.79% 1.17% 2.40%
entries.derivation: Value = column (3), the simulation column (0.006): 4.01 pp × 0.006 = 2.4%, the long-run effect in Table 4. Low and high = the lowest and highest of columns (1)–(3) (0.006 and 0.008).
entries.notes: The paper says further work is needed "to pin down through which policies openness impact on MFP" (p. 16), so a tariff change must first be translated into openness by the user. Harrod-neutral MFP: enter as labour-augmenting (A-P18).

entries.label: Check: real GDP effect of removing all tariffs and their compliance costs (PC National, B7tar)

citation.title: National Competition Policy: modelling proposed reforms (study report with appendices)
citation.locator: Table 6, row B7 'For tariffs', p. 18 (PDF p. 24); Table C.5, row B7tar, p. 222 (PDF p. 228)

entries.quote: For tariffs: GDP: +$3,346–6,691 m (+0.13–0.25%) … Modelled shocks: Removal of all tariffs and increase multifactor productivity (labour and capital) across all industries by 0.06% (representing the removal of the associated compliance costs).
entries.derivation: Low and high = the PC's range (+0.13% to +0.25%); value = the midpoint (0.19).
entries.notes: The simulation combines tariff removal with a +0.06% MFP shock in all industries for the compliance costs of the tariff system (midpoint saving $2.58 billion of $1.29–3.87 billion), so a back-test of tariff removal alone must leave that shock out or add it. The low end is the PC's 50% case. CGE result from PC National (long-run closure).

entries.label: Elasticity of bilateral inward FDI stocks to the OECD FDI Regulatory Restrictiveness Index
entries.units: elasticity (% change in FDI stock per % change in the index)

citation.title: The determinants of Foreign Direct Investment: Do statutory restrictions matter?
citation.publisher: OECD Working Papers on International Investment, 2019/01
citation.locator: Executive summary, p. 8; Table 3, Panel A, column [1], row FDI_RIj,t-1, p. 41

entries.quote: It is estimated that the introduction of reforms leading to a 10% reduction in level of FDI restrictiveness as measured by the Index could increase bilateral FDI inward stocks by around 2.1% on average.
entries.derivation: Value = the Table 3 coefficient (−0.208; 10% × 0.208 ≈ 2.1%). Range = its 95% interval: the t-statistic of −2.82 gives a standard error of 0.0738, so −0.208 ± 1.96 × 0.0738.
entries.notes: Poisson pseudo-maximum-likelihood gravity model. Reported as an investment effect only: no verified FDI-to-MFP elasticity exists (traceability F-C10-03). Effects are larger for services; for M&A, a 10% cut is associated with +3% economy-wide and +3.9% in services (p. 8).
